items.note: The page shows Phi is a well-defined algebra isomorphism (order-S argument), derives the triangular coordinate formula, explains the d,...,1 update order with prefix-controlled shifts, and totals O(d^2) chunk interchanges to reach O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)), following the paper (lines 4197-4292).
A definition, given in full: "Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ ... and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$", with the s_i pairwise coprime and S their product, as in the paper.
The page defines Phi and justifies well-definedness: "Since $s_i\mid S$, each $x_i^{\mu_iS}=1$, so $\Phi$ respects $x^S=1$", which is the reason behind the paper's bare assertion.

The page proves the order is S: Phi(x^k)=1 iff s_i | mu_i k for all i, iff s_i | k (mu_i a unit), iff S | k (pairwise coprime); then the S distinct powers exhaust the S target monomials, so Phi is an isomorphism. This matches the paper's reasoning.
The page writes k in mixed radix with 0<=a_j<s_j, notes b_i = mu_i k mod s_i, and derives b_i=a_i+mu_i sum_{j<i} a_j P_j (mod s_i), as in eq. (triangular-crt).
"Terms with $j>i$ vanish modulo $s_i$, since $s_i$ divides $P_j$, and $\mu_iP_i\equiv1$ modulo $s_i$": both of the paper's reasons are given, with the divisibility made explicit.

dropped: the convention that the update is the identity when any lower-index control is invalid (paper line 4263-4264)
items.note: The page explains that reversing to (a_1,...,a_d) puts controls first and that updating i=d,...,1 leaves lower controls unchanged, so offsets use the original digits. It also notes the shift rotates [0,s_i) and fixes [s_i,t_i), "so zero padding stays zero". It omits the paper's rule for invalid controls.

The page cites the O(V ell^tau) equal-width chunk interchange, handles widths ell vs ell-1 with a fixed number of linear passes, counts O(d^2) moves, and notes that shifts O(dTp), scans O(Tp) and offsets o(Tp) are dominated, giving O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)) for the map, its inverse and the padding.

errors.quote: where $r=2^\ell$ is the record length, so $\ell$ is the number of address bits of an axis of length $r$
errors.problem: r is not a record length. The paper defines r=2^{ceil(log_2 T / d)}, the largest axis length and the polynomial length of R_r=C[y]/(y^r+1) (lines 4058-4059, 1788). Records have O(p) bits, as the page itself says a sentence later, and r grows faster than any fixed power of p. So the page misstates the definition of r.
